stem: The populations of two neighboring towns, in thousands, are modeled by lines of best fit. Town P is modeled by \(12.4 + 0.3t\) and Town Q by \(18.0 - 0.4t\), where \(t\) is the number of years after 2015. What is the least integer value of \(t\) for which the model predicts that the population of Town P is more than 2 thousand greater than the population of Town Q?

explanation.A: Incorrect. This solves \(0.7t > 2\), ignoring that Town P starts 5.6 thousand behind Town Q.
explanation.B: Correct. The difference \(0.7t - 5.6\) first exceeds 2 when \(t > 10.86\), so the least integer is 11.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This rounds \(10.86\) down. At \(t = 10\) the difference is \(7 - 5.6 = 1.4\) thousand, not more than 2.
explanation.D: Incorrect. At \(t = 8\) the two models predict the same population. Town P must then gain another 2 thousand.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'A': 'A', 'D': 'B', 'C': 'C', 'B': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'A', 'B': 'D', 'C': 'C', 'D': 'B'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
P = lambda t: Rational(124, 10) + Rational(3, 10)*t
Q = lambda t: 18 - Rational(4, 10)*t
t = next(t for t in range(0, 100) if P(t) - Q(t) > 2)
assert t == 11 and P(8) == Q(8)
assert value(choices[answer]) == t
assert all(value(choices[k]) != t for k in choices if k != answer)
